_readme: Every value here is invented. No name, address, domain, message or
timestamp is copied from a real submission, and nothing in this file is
derived from production data — the scenarios reproduce the SHAPES seen in
the August 2026 contact-form incident, not its contents. Domains use the
RFC 2606 reserved example.* names plus mainstream providers, because the
mailbox provider is deliberately not a signal.
Each scenario states the shape, the corpus it is scored against, and the
decision the classifier must reach. `corpus` entries are other submissions
that exist alongside the one being scored.

scenarios.why: An ordinary first-time enquiry. One name, one address, real wording.

record.name: Dana Whitfield
record.subject: Question about audit pricing
record.message: Hello, we run a mid-sized logistics firm and would like to understand what an EcoIQ emissions audit covers and roughly what it costs. Are you able to send a summary?

scenarios.why: Free providers carry no signal — real customers and the incident both used them. Must not be penalised.

record.name: Priya Raghunathan
record.subject: Following up on the demo
record.message: Hi there, I attended the webinar last week and wanted to ask whether the reporting module can export to CSV as well as PDF. Thanks very much for your time.

scenarios.why: Brevity is not spam. A short, specific enquiry must survive.

record.name: Tomasz Wiśniewski
record.subject: Integration
record.message: Does the API support webhook callbacks on audit completion?

scenarios.why: The August 2026 shape: a single contact name behind dozens of unrelated addresses. Decisive on its own.

record.name: Alex Morgan
record.subject: Business proposal
record.message: Good day, I represent an investment group interested in discussing a partnership opportunity with your organisation at your earliest convenience.

corpus_generator.name: Alex Morgan
corpus_generator.subject: Business proposal
corpus_generator.message_template: Good day, I represent investment group {i} and would like to discuss a partnership opportunity with your organisation.

scenarios.why: A name on a handful of addresses is ordinary — a shared team inbox, a resent enquiry. Weak alone, so it must not reject and must not review on its own.

record.name: Sam Okonkwo
record.subject: Renewal question
record.message: Hello, our procurement team asked me to check whether the annual licence renews automatically or needs a new purchase order each year.

corpus_generator.name: Sam Okonkwo
corpus_generator.subject: Renewal question
corpus_generator.message_template: Hello, our procurement team asked me to check point {i} of the renewal terms before the purchase order is raised.

scenarios.why: One message body sent from many different addresses under different names. Decisive on its own — the name rule alone would miss it.

record.name: Chris Bell
record.subject: Collaboration

corpus_generator.subject: Collaboration
corpus_generator.message: Dear team we noticed your website and would like to offer our services for improving your search rankings please reply for our rate card

scenarios.why: An identical resubmission is suspicious but a real person double-clicks. One MEDIUM signal reviews, it does not reject.

record.name: Helen Marsh
record.subject: Audit scope
record.message: Could you confirm whether scope 3 supply chain emissions are included in the standard audit package or charged separately?

scenarios.why: A throwaway inbox plus near-empty wording. Neither rejects alone; together they warrant a human look.

record.name: J
record.subject: hi
record.message: test test test test test test

scenarios.why: A malformed address and a wall of links. Two MEDIUM signals together are enough to reject without any cross-record evidence.
